preHero.mainHeadline: Don't read this if you're okay with your talented child being bored in school surrounded by average peers...
preHero.mainSubtext: But if you want to give them an elite environment and a portfolio that makes Ivy League admission committees speechless — read every word.
preHero.subheadline1: If you're a parent who doesn't want your smart child to become just another faceless content consumer, unable to create anything of value...

preHero.conclusion: Then this letter will change the trajectory of their life.
preHero.intro: My name is Alex. I own three businesses, judge startup competitions, and mentor entrepreneurs. And over the past 2 years, I've realized something important...
preHero.storyTitle: Let me tell you about Daniel.
preHero.storyP1: At 12, he was a regular middle schooler. Got straight A's. Played Minecraft. Asked his parents to buy him another $20 in-game purchase.
preHero.storyP2: His mom Kate was desperate. She saw her son's potential but didn't know how to unlock it. Coding classes? Boring after a month. Robotics? Same story.
preHero.storyP3: Then she discovered MBA for Kids.
preHero.storyItem1: Built a pocket money management app (a real working product)
preHero.storyItem2: Pitched to 6 investors at a competition
preHero.storyItem3: Earned his first $800 selling subscriptions to classmates
preHero.storyItem4: Got invited to a pre-incubator program at the local university
preHero.storyP5: But you know what matters most?
preHero.quoteIntro: When I asked Kate, "What changed in Daniel?" she cried and said:
preHero.quoteMain: He stopped being a child who asks. He became a person who creates.
preHero.storyConclusion: That's what we do at MBA for Kids.

problem.title: Is Your Child Prepared for a World That Doesn't Play by the Rules?
problem.subtitle: The world is changing faster than the school system. While other kids are building the future, is yours just consuming it?
problem.card1Text: Imagine your child not just watching videos, but building the next viral app. Every hour spent scrolling is an hour they could spend creating something that matters. The good news? It's not too late to shift from passive consumer to active creator.
problem.card2Text: While schools focus on memorizing facts, successful kids are learning to build, pitch, and sell. Your child has the potential to understand money, create digital products, and think like an entrepreneur. They just need the right environment to unlock it.
problem.card3Text: Every child who launches their first project experiences a transformation. They stand taller. Speak clearer. Believe in themselves. That confidence doesn't come from participation trophies—it comes from building something real and presenting it to the world.
problem.card4Text: Ages 11-14 are the prime years for developing entrepreneurial thinking. Miss this window, and it becomes exponentially harder later. But catch it now, and you're setting your child up with skills that compound for life.
problem.card5Text: Right now, thousands of kids are learning to code, launching businesses, and building portfolios. The gap grows every month. But here's the inspiring part: your child can join them. They can be the one with a real project, real skills, and a real competitive edge.
problem.ctaText: In 4 months, your child will either have a working project they're proud of and skills that set them apart... or they'll still be wondering 'what if?'
